The closest GRU-compatible result is [2Gated-TimeGRU, HICSS 2024](https://aisel.aisnet.org/hicss-57/da/data_science/10/). It incorporates intervals between consecutive interactions into a time-sensitive GRU architecture to capture short-term preferences and interest evolution. Authors report improved recommendation accuracy on real datasets; this supports testing explicit elapsed-time conditioning within the existing recurrent backbone. [FMRES, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104070) combines personalized forgetting curves, memory replay and GRU temporal modeling. Its full architecture requires social relationships and rating-derived information unavailable here; the transferable idea is jointly learned retention sensitive to elapsed time.

Practical experiment suggested by these findings, rather than a verified reproduction: condition GRU reset/update gates on transformed inter-event gaps, or apply learned positive-rate decay to the previous hidden state before the GRU update. Compare against the corrected baseline using macro validation HR@10; gains on this benchmark remain unproven. Learn decay jointly with item embeddings and recurrence in one network per category. Preserve hidden state across padding, calculate gaps only between real historical events, and read the final nonpadding position—never count−1 for left-padded histories. Use only timestamps available at prediction time; avoid dependence on the unknown next-interaction timestamp. Keep the same temporal features, architecture and checkpoint loading in training, diagnosis and the embedded predictor.
